upstream: DigestDef.Algorithm (MD2, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512)
evidence: run: packages/bundle-standard/test/digest-tika.test.ts reproduces the digests Tika's DigestConfigTest hard-codes for test_recursive_embedded.docx: MD2 d768c8e2..., MD5 59f626e0..., SHA1, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512 and SHA3-512; packages/core/test/digest.test.ts checks MD2 against RFC 1319's suite and the rest against NIST/hashlib answers
note: All 9. node:crypto has md5, sha1, sha2 and sha3; MD2 is not in OpenSSL 3, so it is ripstream's own (RFC 1319). Measured: MD2 5.2 MiB/s, MD5 602, SHA-256 2,421, SHA3-512 466; MD2 is for parity, and SHA-256 is the one to use for large documents.

upstream: DigestDef.Encoding (HEX default, BASE32, BASE64)
evidence: run: digest.test.ts checks hex (lower case), BASE64 and BASE32 against RFC 4648 with padding; digest-tika.test.ts matches Tika's SHA1 BASE32 PIPQAHIWHLEQ3DVFJQCQ7L22HADZPCFG; the CLI printed the same value under tk:digest:SHA-1:BASE32 in-process and under strict isolation
note: Key suffix rule: hex is bare tk:digest:<ALG>, others append :BASE32/:BASE64.

upstream: CommonsDigester (JCA MessageDigest; MD2..SHA-512; rejects SHA3)
evidence: run: digest-config.test.ts: commons-digester-factory refuses SHA3_256/384/512 with the message that points to bouncy-castle-digester-factory, as CommonsDigester.checkSupported does; `ripstream metadata -c` with it exits 2
note: MD2..SHA-512 on node:crypto and Md2.

upstream: BouncyCastleDigester (SHA3-256/384/512 via BC)
evidence: run: digest-tika.test.ts: bouncy-castle-digester-factory with MD5, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512 and SHA3_512 gives Tika's expected values and writes no MD2
note: SHA3 is node:crypto's (sha3-256/384/512); no BouncyCastle.

upstream: InputStreamDigester (reads the whole stream; digest() and digestSink(); rewinds the TikaInputStream)
evidence: run: digest.test.ts: one pass over every byte from the stream's position to its end whatever the chunks, the position put back, a temp-file-spooled document digested the same, Content-Length set only where blank, an abort stops it
note: Not carried: digestSink (see dig-sinks) and CacheMemoryBudget/tryRetainInMemory, which are Java stream details; RipstreamInputStream spools to memory and then a temporary file.

upstream: CompositeDigester (runs N digesters in sequence, stream rewound between)
evidence: run: digest.test.ts: SHA256 hex, MD5 BASE64 and SHA256 BASE32 in one pass give three keys in the configured order
note: Tika rewinds between digesters; one pass feeds every algorithm, which gives the same values.

upstream: CommonsDigesterFactory (parse-context key commons-digester-factory; config: digests[{algorithm,encoding}], skipContainerDocumentDigest=false)
evidence: run: digest-config.test.ts reads Tika's tika-config-digests.json, -skip-container.json and the empty factory (MD5, hex); refuses unknown settings, bad shapes and both factories at once; reads enums in any case as Tika's mapper does
note: `parse-context` `commons-digester-factory`: digests[{algorithm, encoding}], skipContainerDocumentDigest. Reaches createRipstream, the isolation child (IsolatedComponents.digest) and pipes (PipesSettings.digest).

upstream: BouncyCastleDigesterFactory (bouncy-castle-digester-factory)
evidence: run: digest-config.test.ts: tika-config-bc-digests-multiple.json (MD5, SHA256, SHA3_512) is read
note: Same settings as the commons factory, and SHA3 allowed.

upstream: DigestHelper.maybeDigest + SkipContainerDocumentDigest marker (digest container before parse unless skipContainerDocumentDigest; embedded docs digested at depth>0; depth null/0 = container)
ripstream: packages/core/src/parser.ts (AutoDetectParser.parse calls maybeDigest before detection); packages/pipes/src/index.ts (NO_PARSE)
evidence: run: digest-tika.test.ts and digest.test.ts: with skipContainerDocumentDigest the container has no digest and every embedded record has one, without it all do; standard-isolation.test.ts: the same across the isolation boundary; modes.test.ts: NO_PARSE with the option digests nothing
note: Digest runs in AutoDetectParser before the type is detected, for the container and every embedded document, at depth from CONTEXT_KEYS.EMBEDDED_DEPTH (depth 0 is the container). Tika's pipes digest the container first and mark it so the parser does not repeat it; the digests are the same, made once.

upstream: DigestSink / BufferingDigestSink (digest embedded bytes while a parser streams them)
evidence: source: DigestSink/BufferingDigestSink digest the bytes of an embedded OLE2/PST stream as the parser writes them, which saves a second read; ripstream digests the document's own stored bytes when it enters AutoDetectParser
note: The values are the same where the bytes are; only the second read differs, and RipstreamInputStream spools so it is cheap. Proposed as a non-goal until an owner decision.

upstream: MSEmbeddedStreamTranslator, PSTEmailStreamTranslator, DefaultEmbeddedStreamTranslator (EmbeddedStreamTranslator SPI; NOT language translators)
evidence: run: `ripstream -r -c <md5 config> test_recursive_embedded.docx` digests the embedded /oleObject1.bin (13,824 bytes) as it enters the parser; source: MSEmbeddedStreamTranslator re-serialises OLE2 through POI and PSTEmailStreamTranslator writes nothing, so Tika's digests of those documents are of bytes ripstream does not produce
note: Deviation: an embedded OLE2 or oleObject document is digested as extracted, not as POI re-writes it, and an email in a PST gets the digest of nothing in Tika. Not reproducible here (no Java to run Tika). Tika's own test asserts only that embedded records have a digest, not its value.

note: Hex is bare, others append :BASE32 or :BASE64; the name is the JCA one (SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA3-512).
